archival_prior.detectors: n6,n7,n9,b1 (4, all blocks) - identical to the GBM catalog SCAT mask and to Yu+2019's analysed set

detail.time_resolved_blocks_0_to_8: ZERO pass either nested test. Best in class: LRT_BANDBB_BAND = 6.20 (blk7, 7.78-10.54 s, kT = 2.97 keV) and LRT_CPLBB_CPL = 4.02 (same block). Both are far below the 9.2 threshold.
detail.integrated_[-1.00,15.00]s: CPL+BB pair ONLY: LRT_CPLBB_CPL = 11.61, kT_CplBB = 42.99 +- 7.48 keV (CPLBB_VALID = True) -> passes. The Band+BB pair in the SAME interval gives LRT_BANDBB_BAND = -2.1e-06 (i.e. exactly zero improvement) with kT railed at 1.014 keV and BANDBB_VALID = False. A textbook live instance of the T8/union-rule baseline-dependence: the 'ΔAIC for a blackbody' here is entirely a statement about which continuum it was measured against.
detail.why_the_integrated_pass_is_suspect: kT = 42.99 keV with MINOS errors NaN (CPLBB_KT_NEG_ERR / POS_ERR both nan), sitting alongside a nearly identical kT = 43.02 keV in blk2 - a repeated parameter value across unrelated intervals is a local-minimum / seed signature, not two independent temperature measurements. AIC ordering in the integrated block is CPL+BB 5569.57 < CPL 5577.18 < SBPL 5577.57 < DSBPL 5577.64 < Band 5578.06 < Band+BB 5582.06.

archival_prior.kT_floor_railing_note: 6 of the 20 BB fits land within 0.2 keV of 1.0 keV (1.014, 1.022, 1.031, 1.076, 1.095, 1.193) - i.e. railed at the kT floor. These are 'no blackbody found', not 'a 1 keV blackbody found'. This is precisely what the kT > 1.05 guard in the union rule exists to catch, and it is doing its job here.
archival_prior.beta_railing_note: BAND_BETA rails at exactly -5.000 in blocks 0, 2 and 6 - a BOUND_CAPPED signature (L9 class). In all three the AIC winner is CPL or Band+BB rather than Band, consistent with Band's high-energy index carrying no information in those intervals. The L9 hardening (widen caps + diagnose BOUND_CAPPED) should change these three blocks if anything does.
archival_prior.break_structure: LRT_DSBPL_SBPL never reaches 9.2. Max = 7.36 (blk6, 6.95-7.78 s) but DSBPL_VALID = False there; the integrated block gives 3.93 with DSBPL_VALID = True. Two SBPL AIC wins (blk4 4.71-6.02 s and blk5 6.02-6.95 s), both spanning the pulse peak; blk4 is also the BIC winner. So the archival prior sees SINGLE-break structure at the peak and NO valid two-break block anywhere.

external_binning_corroboration.claim: the archival Bayesian Blocks reproduce Yu+2019's independently published block edges
external_binning_corroboration.agreement: 8 of 8 interior edges match to Yu's printed 2 decimals. The only Yu edge we lack is 9.05, which in their Table 21 produces a ZERO-WIDTH bin (9.05->9.05, S = 5.2) - an artifact, not a change point.
external_binning_corroboration.independence_caveat: NOT fully independent - both use Bayesian Blocks on the brightest NaI with p0 = 0.01 (Yu+2019 Sec 2.3). But the implementations (3ML vs theirs), the background models, the detector windows (-1..15 vs -5..20 s) and the analysts differ, so the agreement is still a real external check on Step 5.

predictions: P-A (Ep track, prompt-scope): after frame alignment (all comparisons in nuFnu-peak Ep, photon-index sign, GBM 8 keV-40 MeV, T0 = 340559125.719054 MET), the fresh blind Ep(t) lands inside the published envelope in every constrained block: ~0.8-3.6 s Ep in 700-1400 keV; the Ep MAXIMUM in the 3.6-4.7 s block at 850-950 keV; the pulse-peak block 4.71-6.02 s at 450-620 keV (Yu CPL 559 / Yu Band 486 / catalog pflx-Comp 476 over 5.12-6.14 s / archival CPL_EPK 541 / archival BAND_EP 436); 6.0-7.8 s decaying through 300-360 keV; and the last block 10.5-15.0 s at 150-250 keV. FALSIFIER: an Ep(t) that decays STRICTLY MONOTONICALLY from the first constrained block would side with Lu+2018's 'H' class and against Yu+2019's 'h.t.s. to s.t.h.'; a value outside these ranges by more than the published errors in any S>=20-equivalent block is a genuine diff item, not a rounding difference.

P-A2 (the late Ep rebound - the sharpest published disagreement): Yu+2019 see Ep RISE from 303 keV (6.95-7.78 s) back to 528 keV (7.78-9.05 s), which is the entire basis of their 's.t.h.' second phase. Our archival prior does NOT reproduce it: block 7 (7.78-10.54 s) gives CPL_EPK = 362 keV and BAND_EP = 337 keV, i.e. continued decay. The blocks are NOT the same (we merge across Yu's 9.05 change point), so this may be pure binning. PREDICTION: if the fresh Step-5 binning splits at ~9.05 s, the 7.78-9.05 s block shows Ep >= 450 keV and the class is 'h.t.s. to s.t.h.'; if it does not split there, the merged block sits at 330-420 keV and we CANNOT adjudicate Lu vs Yu - and must say so rather than pick. FALSIFIER for the whole item: a split block at 7.78-9.05 s with Ep <= 380 keV would contradict Yu+2019 directly and make Lu+2018's 'H' the better description.

P-B (BB / union rule): the L18+ engine finds ZERO or ONE time-resolved block passing the union rule. The archival prior finds ZERO (best LRT_BANDBB = 6.20, best LRT_CPLBB = 4.02, both in blk7), with six of twenty BB fits railed at the kT floor. FALSIFIER / UPSIDE: if the fresh run yields >= 2 time-resolved blocks passing, the archival zero was a pre-L18 seed/cap artifact (L8/L9 class) AND - because no paper has ever fitted a thermal component to this burst - it is a genuinely new, literature-silent result that must clear L28's detector-coherence acquittal before it is called physics. SEPARATE FALSIFIER: the integrated-block CPL+BB pass (LRT 11.61, kT 42.99 +- 7.48 keV, MINOS errors NaN, and kT = 43.02 keV repeated in blk2) is predicted NOT to survive as a physical photosphere - it should be diagnosed as curvature that Band's beta absorbs (the Band+BB pair in the same interval improves by exactly zero). If instead it survives with finite MINOS errors and a kT that is NOT ~43 keV in a second interval, the prior was wrong and the integrated thermal component is real.

P-C (shape / break structure): ZERO blocks reach LRT_DSBPL_SBPL >= 9.2 with DSBPL_VALID = True. The archival maximum is 7.36 in blk6 with DSBPL_VALID = False. But SBPL wins on AIC in blocks 4 and 5 (4.71-6.95 s, spanning the pulse peak) and on BIC in block 4, so the prediction is SINGLE-break structure at the peak and NO valid two-break block. FALSIFIER: any block with LRT_DSBPL_SBPL >= 9.2 AND DSBPL_VALID = True is a two-break detection with no literature precedent whatsoever for this burst - which raises the bar, not lowers it: it must survive the L8 default-seed DSBPL restart before it is counted.

P-D (binning, testable independently of any fit): the fresh Step-5 Bayesian Blocks reproduce at least 6 of Yu+2019's 8 published interior edges (0.77, 2.68, 3.60, 4.71, 6.02, 6.95, 7.78, 10.54 s) to within 0.05 s. The archival prior matched 8 of 8. FALSIFIER: fewer than 6 matches means our binning changed materially between engine eras and the Step-5 comparison to Yu+2019 must be re-derived before any Step-6 diff is trusted.

P-E (model family, from the catalog anchor): the GBM catalog prefers Comptonized (CPL) over Band for BOTH the fluence and the peak-flux spectrum, and Band's beta is unconstrained there (-2.894 +- 4.431). PREDICTION: CPL is the AIC or BIC winner in a majority of the fresh time-resolved blocks (archival: BIC 8/9 blocks, AIC 4/9). FALSIFIER: Band winning the majority would put us against both the official catalog and our own prior, and would need explaining before anything else in this burst is reported.
